paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's word doesn't need your permission to stay true. Jehoiakim cut that scroll up and fed it to the fire, and he thought the problem went up in smoke with it. But burning a warning doesn't cancel it. It just means the one who burned it hears the same thing again, with more added (Jer 36:23, 32).

Now look at why God sent those words in the first place. He said, "Perhaps when the people of Judah hear about all the calamity I plan to bring upon them, each of them will turn from his wicked way. Then I will forgive their iniquity and their sin" (Jer 36:3). A warning from God is an open door, not a trap. And notice who got scared and who didn't: the officials turned to one another in fear (Jer 36:16), but the king and his servants "did not become frightened or tear their garments" (Jer 36:24).

So here's what I'd carry out of my bakery today, baker. When God's word stings, don't reach for the firepot. Listen, turn and let Him forgive, because the One who made a new scroll out of ashes is still the One who wants to forgive you. And I know a little something about God not leaving a good thing in the dark, so trust me: when He speaks, you want to be the one who listens.
